newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ monetary conditions index rises in Sept - BTNZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ monetary conditions index rises in Sept - BTNZ.

text.p: Bankers Trust New Zealand said on Thursday its monetary conditions index rose slightly to average 133.5 in September from 127.5 in August.
The MCI rose steadily during the month as the Trade Weighted Index appreciated, finishing September above 138.
BTNZ said the assumed MCI for the December quarter, based on the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's September economic projections, was 126.

BTNZ said the strength of the currency during September reflected a number of factors, including the RBNZ's decision to keep monetary policy on hold in their September projections, with 90-day bank bill rates assumed unchanged at 10 percent.
It also reflected continued retail interest in New Zealand fixed interest products from Europe and Japan, with samurai and eurokiwi issuance in 1996 closing in on NZ$5 billion.
Finally, the U.S. Federal Reserve's decision to leave interest rates unchanged at the September 24 FOMC meeting had added to the attractiveness of New Zealand yields.

BTNZ said the given the RBNZ's decision to ease only when it sees "conclusive evidence" that inflation pressures have turned, data since the bank's September projections had been generally neutral to positive for the inflation outlook.
"Wages are a notable exception, however, with private sector wage growth accelerating to four percent in the year to May."
BTNZ said an easing in monetary conditions beginning in December was still on track, provided data due in the interim continued its moderate tone.
"The 12 October election may, of course, overshadow all of this," it warned.

"A change of government would almost certainly mean more government spending and a less aggressive anti-inflation policy. Based on current polls, the election result is still 'too close to call'," BTNZ said.
